chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, from Sa'd b. 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa and Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi al-Khattab, from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, who said: I read the letter of Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him):

Convey to my Shi'a that my visitation equals in the sight of Allah a thousand Hajj pilgrimages. He (al-Bazanti) said: So I said to Abu Ja'far, his son (peace be upon him): A thousand Hajj? He said: Yes, by Allah, and a million Hajj pilgrimages for whoever visits him recognizing his right.

key_terms.حجة: Hajj pilgrimage — one of the five pillars of Islam
key_terms.زيارة: Visitation (ziyara) — pilgrimage to an Imam's shrine
key_terms.عارفاً بحقه: Recognizing his right — acknowledging his divinely appointed Imamate

ai.seo_question: How many Hajj pilgrimages does visiting Imam al-Rida equal?
ai.summary: Al-Bazanti read a letter from Imam al-Rida (AS) which stated: 'Convey to my Shi'a that my visitation equals in the sight of Allah a thousand Hajj pilgrimages.' When al-Bazanti asked Imam al-Jawad (AS) — al-Rida's son — about this, he confirmed: 'Yes, by Allah, and a million Hajj pilgrimages for whoever visits him recognizing his right.' This hadith emphasizes the extraordinary spiritual reward of visiting Imam al-Rida's shrine with knowledge of his true status as a divinely appointed Imam.
